<<NOTES ON FRAMING OF A BARN DOOR>>

A BARN DOOR IS MADE OF TWO PLANKS THAT ARE JOINED WITH A TIE OR A ROD TO KEEP THEM ALIGNED. THE PLANKS ARE CUT TO THE SAME WIDTH AND LENGTH TO MAKE THEM FIT TOGETHER. THE TIE IS INSERTED BETWEEN THE PLANKS TO HOLD THEM IN PLACE. THE TIE IS THEN DRILLED WITH HOLE TO FIT A NAIL OR A SCREW. THE NAILS OR SCREWS ARE INSERTED INTO THE HOLE AND THE PLANKS ARE BOLTED TOGETHER. THE BARN DOOR IS FITTED TO THE FRAME OF THE BARN WITH A ROD OR A TIE TO ALIGN IT. THE ROD OR TIE IS THEN DRILLED WITH HOLE TO FIT A NAIL OR SCREW. THE NAILS OR SCREWS ARE INSERTED INTO THE HOLE AND THE BARN DOOR IS BOLTED TO THE FRAME. THE BARN DOOR IS THEN CHECKED TO MAKE SURE IT IS LEVEL AND STRAIGHT.
